 Medicare plan volatility leaves older Clark County residents with fewer choices, higher prices
 Insurance brokers say they also are being squeezed
 By
 Kimberly Cortez, Staff writer 
 November 19, 2026  8:03 am 
 Clark County , Government , Health , News 
 Licensed Medicare insurance broker Timothy Jones works at his desk Thursday at The Baldwin Group Health Insurance in east Vancouver. (Photos by Taylor Balkom/The Columbian)
 A flag stands outside of The Baldwin Group Health Insurance in east Vancouver on Thursday.
 The Baldwin Group Health Insurance is in east Vancouver. (Taylor Balkom/The Columbian)
 Licensed Medicare insurance broker Timothy Jones stands for a portrait Thursday at The Baldwin Group Health Insurance in east Vancouver. (taylor balkom/The Columbian)

 Open enrollment is underway for 2027 Washington Medicare plans. Older adults in Clark County can expect fewer private plans, higher out-of-pocket maximums and less flexibility.
 About 64,632 Clark County residents were enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan before the enrollment period began in mid-October, according to data from Vlada Health. There’s still time to pick a plan before enrollment ends Dec. 7, but insurance brokers warn residents to expect a volatile market.
